subject: computing
title: Recursion: factorial(4) — the Call Stack Grows, Then Unwinds

questions.prompt: When factorial(4) calls factorial(3), what happens to the factorial(4) call?

choices.text: It returns 24 immediately, before factorial(3) runs
It is suspended on the call stack, holding its place and its pending multiplication, and resumes when factorial(3) returns
It is deleted from memory so factorial(3) can take its place
It restarts from the beginning once factorial(3) finishes

questions.misconception: A recursive call replaces the caller, so factorial(4) is finished and gone once factorial(3) starts.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: A recursive call replaces the caller, so factorial(4) is finished and gone once factorial(3) starts. In fact The caller is not replaced: it is suspended on the call stack, still holding its place and its pending multiplication, and it resumes exactly where it stopped when the callee returns - which is why the stack unwinds in reverse order, multiplying 1, 2, 6, 24.

questions.prompt: Which call is the base case in the factorial(4) trace, and what does it do?

choices.text: factorial(4): it calls nothing and returns 24
factorial(1): it calls nothing and returns 1
factorial(2): it calls nothing and returns 2
There is no base case; the calls descend for ever

questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: factorial(1) is the base case - it calls nothing, pushes no new frame, and returns 1 at once, which stops the descent.

questions.prompt: A student claims that once factorial(3) starts, nothing of factorial(4) remains. Explain, in two sentences, what actually happens to the factorial(4) call.
questions.answer: The caller is not replaced: it is suspended on the call stack, still holding its place and its pending multiplication, and it resumes exactly where it stopped when the callee returns - which is why the stack unwinds in reverse order, multiplying 1, 2, 6, 24.
questions.explanation: The deciding habit is to keep every caller on the stack: each call pauses with its multiplication still pending, and the frames can only complete in reverse order as the callees return.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state what factorial(1) returns and why the descent stops there.
questions.answer: factorial(1) is the base case: it calls nothing and returns 1, so no new frame is pushed and the stack starts to unwind.
questions.explanation: Scene 2 shows the base case answering directly: with no further call made, the deepest frame returns and the unwind can begin.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the stages of the factorial(4) evaluation in order?

choices.text: factorial(4) pauses and calls factorial(3), factorial(3) pauses and calls factorial(2), factorial(2) pauses and calls factorial(1), the base case returns 1, then the frames resume in reverse and multiply 1, 2, 6, 24
factorial(4) returns 24 first, then factorial(3), factorial(2) and factorial(1) run in that order
factorial(1) runs first and calls factorial(2), which calls factorial(3), which calls factorial(4)
The base case returns 24, then the stack grows as factorial(2), factorial(3) and factorial(4) are called

questions.explanation: Scene 1 stacks the calls downwards, scene 2 reaches the base case returning 1, scene 3 unwinds the frames multiplying in reverse, and scene 4 returns 24 from the outermost frame.
